issues.problem: `scanBlocks` moves the cursor forward before it runs the operation. Only the UNLOADED result moves it back. When the result is NO_OUTPUT_SPACE (output full), the target block has already been passed, so it stays unmined for the rest of the pass. FAILED results also just continue: a replacer with an empty or non-block replacement slot passes over every block in the area without replacing any.
issues.reason: The AC says only allowed coordinates are handled and that replacement counts match. A machine that silently passes over blocks when its output is full or its material runs out leaves the area partly unprocessed, and the counts no longer match the area.
issues.fix: Move the cursor forward only after SUCCESS, NO_TARGET or a filter rejection. For NO_OUTPUT_SPACE, and for the replacer having no usable replacement item, keep the cursor on the current target and stop with a status such as OUTPUT_FULL or NO_MATERIAL.

issues.problem: The replacer breaks the target through `BlockOperationService`, then places the new block with a plain `serverLevel.setBlockAndUpdate(target, blockItem.getBlock().defaultBlockState())`. Nothing checks permission to place there. No `BlockEvent.EntityPlaceEvent` is fired, `canSurvive` and placement state are not checked, and the owner FakePlayer is not used for the placement.
issues.reason: The AC says protected targets are not changed. Protection mods cancel placement through the NeoForge place event, which is skipped here. The default state can also be invalid at the target (for example a torch with nothing to attach to).
issues.fix: Place the block through the owner FakePlayer with `BlockItem.place(new BlockPlaceContext(...))`, or fire `EventHooks.onBlockPlace`/`EntityPlaceEvent`, then check the result. Consume the replacement item only on success. If placement is denied, return DENIED without breaking the original block first: check placement before the break or simulate it.

issues.problem: The scan speeds (1/1/4/1/1 operations per tick, no CE cost) and the laser bonus formula `max(1, floor(beam.energy()))` in `AreaMachineBlockEntity.acceleratedOperations` have no cited source in the original hotfix2 classes (TileAreaMiner, TileAdvancedAreaMiner, TileAreaCollector, TileAreaReplacer, TileAreaActivator). Speed comes from the machine type, not the Tier, and no machine uses any Clay Energy.

issues.fix: Read the original area machine classes. Copy their per-Tier progress, energy consumption and laser acceleration formula into `AreaMachineType` and `acceleratedOperations`, adding CE consumption and a fuel slot if the original has them. Record the values and their source in AGENTS.md, and have the GameTest assert the exact values.

issues.problem: The test checks acceleration by calling `acceleratedOperations(new LaserBeam(...))` directly. It never delivers a beam through the `InterfaceCapabilities.LASER_RECEIVER` capability, never toggles the laser, and never measures how many blocks a tick actually processes. Protection is tested only for mining, not for replacement or activation. No test checks that blocks just outside the configured area stay untouched while the machine runs.
issues.reason: The criterion's Action is to run the machines and switch the acceleration condition, and the Expected Result is that only allowed coordinates are changed and protected targets stay unchanged. The assertions cover neither the runtime capability path nor protection for every operation type.
issues.fix: Fill a multi-block area. Get the LaserReceiver capability with `level.getCapability`, deliver a beam, let `serverTick` run, and assert the number of blocks processed with and without the laser equals the exact expected values. Add protected-target cases for the replacer (cancel the place/break event) and the activator. Put sentinel blocks next to the area and assert they are unchanged afterwards.

issues.problem: The test places four marker blocks at Y=-64/0/255/319, then never uses them. It calls `AreaBounds.between` on raw coordinates, never pairs markers or calls `AreaMarkerBlockEntity.selectedArea()`/`configureFromMarker`, and never runs a machine to prove no coordinate outside the range is scanned. The markers are also placed at absolute positions outside the test structure and never removed.
issues.reason: The Preconditions and Action are placing markers at the boundaries and applying the expansion through selection. The 'never scans outside' result needs a real scan. Blocks left outside the structure can leak into other tests.
issues.fix: Place the markers inside the test's reach, or remove them in a finally block. Pair them through the marker API (`select`, or placement with an owner) and read `selectedArea()` from each marker type. Configure a machine from a marker near the build limits and run it until the cursor wraps. Assert that only positions inside `getMinBuildHeight()`..`getMaxBuildHeight()-1` and the selected X/Z were touched, for example with sentinel blocks just outside.

issues.problem: Area machines have no Menu or GUI, so a player cannot place a tool, replacement material or filter into a chosen slot. The only way in is the ItemHandler capability, and `insertItem` accepts slots 0 and 1. Slot 0 accepts any item, so a hopper puts an ItemFilter into the operation slot instead of the filter slot. Right-click gives no feedback when a marker range is or is not applied.
issues.reason: The AC Action is for a player to run the machines with tools, filters and replacement items. Without a way to fill slots 0 and 1 separately, the M10 filter integration cannot be used in play.
issues.fix: Add an area machine Menu and Screen (reuse the existing machine screen base) that exposes slot 0, the filter slot and the outputs, opened from `useWithoutItem`. Alternatively, reject ItemFilter items in slot 0 of the external handler. Show a message when a marker range is applied.

issues.problem: The remembered marker is stored in `Player.getPersistentData()` under hand-made keys. The value is written into the player save permanently and never cleared after use. Pairing (`AreaMarkerBlock.pairWithNearest`: nearest marker of the same type and owner within ±16 blocks, found by scanning 35,937 positions on every placement) and this right-click workflow are documented nowhere.
issues.reason: The project already uses NeoForge Data Attachments for per-player state (M18 `gadget_player_state`). Raw persistent data is the legacy path. Without documentation, the selection rules (radius, same type, owner) cannot be checked against the AC.
issues.fix: Replace the persistent-data keys with a non-serialized Data Attachment, or clear the value after a machine uses it. Document the pairing radius, same-type/owner rule and right-click workflow in the AGENTS.md M30 section. Check that the 16-block search radius matches the original marker range.

issues.problem: The marker model shows `laserreflector.png` (the laser reflector's texture) on its front and `denseclay.png` on its body, and the markers get a horizontal FACING property. Nothing shows that the original markers looked like this. In `AreaMarkerBlock`, the model is a 6×12×6 pillar but the block has no `getShape` override, so its outline and collision are a full cube.
issues.reason: The AC requires original PNGs that let users read the marker. Putting the laser reflector texture on a marker misrepresents the block, the made-up facing adds a state the original did not have, and a full-cube outline around a thin pillar is a wrong boundary display.
issues.fix: Use the texture the original marker blocks used (check the original CBlocks/marker classes) and drop FACING if the original markers had no orientation. Add a VoxelShape override that matches the model in `AreaMarkerBlock`.

issues.problem: Every tick that processes at least one block calls `setChangedAndSync`, sending a full block update to clients. `getUpdateTag` sends `cursor`, `target_dimension` and `status`, but no client code reads them; the renderer only uses `workArea`. Once `status` becomes PROTECTED, UNLOADED or OUTPUT_FULL, it never returns to IDLE.
issues.reason: Syncing data the client does not use, on every working tick, wastes network traffic. A status that sticks after its cause is gone is stale saved state.
issues.fix: Sync only when `workArea` changes (`configureArea`), call plain `setChanged()` during scanning, and put only `area_min`/`area_max` in the update tag. Reset `status` at the start of each `runOperationsNow`.

issues.problem: This screenshot should show the work-range outlines and machine fronts, but it shows neither. The view shows the superflat grass ground far below, with only orange (open-pit) and light-blue/purple (prism) vertical outline edges running into the distance. The smooth-stone platform at y=99, the five area machines with their south-facing fronts and the yellow 3×3×3 work-range boxes are all missing.
issues.reason: The scenario places the camera at x=0.5, y=110, z=14.5. That is outside the platform it builds (fill -12 99 -10 to 12 99 12, so z only goes up to 12). The player is in creative but not flying, so they fall off the platform toward the superflat ground before the shot. The first screenshot also looks like it was taken from about y=101.6 (eye height above the platform) instead of y=104, which means the player is falling there too. As a result, nothing in this image lets a user read the machine directions or work ranges.
issues.fix: In tests/e2e/area-machines.mjs, keep the camera fixed at its scripted position. Either switch to spectator mode, or stand the player on a solid block or an extended platform under the camera position. Then put the second camera inside or above the platform, south of the machines, looking north: for example x=0.5, y=106, z=11.5, yaw 180, pitch about 30, which should show all five fronts and their boxes. Wait a few ticks for chunks to render before the screenshot. Retake the shot and check that all five machines, their fronts and their yellow boxes are visible.

issues.problem: The prism marker (clay_marker_prism at x=0, z=-4) has no outline in this screenshot. No magenta (0.9, 0.2, 1.0) edges rise from or around the 4th marker cube. The other three markers render: the cyan box for the normal marker, the orange top for open-pit and the green vertical edges for ground leveling. So all four marker types can't be read from this image, and the prism range is not drawn.
issues.reason: The prism area runs from y=-64 to 320, so its vertical edges are about 384 blocks long. AreaOutlineRenderer.edge() passes the unnormalized edge vector as the line normal. The vanilla lines shader computes each line's screen direction from Position+Normal, so a far-away end point (behind the camera or outside the clip range) can probably produce a degenerate or invisible quad. This is my best explanation from the code; I didn't confirm it by experiment. The same prism lines do show up (light-blue/purple) in the other screenshot taken from below, which fits a problem that depends on view angle rather than the outline being missing from the data.
issues.fix: In AreaOutlineRenderer.edge(), normalize the normal to unit length, as vanilla LevelRenderer.renderLineBox does. Also split very long edges into segments of about 16–32 blocks so neither end point leaves the view volume. Then retake the screenshot and check that the magenta prism edges are visible above the floor next to the 4th marker, alongside the cyan, orange and green outlines.
